newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sommer block trade fans speculation.
newsitem.headline: Sommer block trade fans speculation.

text.p: A block of shares in diversified equipment manufacturer Sommer-Allibert representing 2.5 percent of its capital was traded on Wednesday, fanning speculation that its auto parts business might draw the interest of large suppliers.
Sommer-Allibert shares which finished up 3.67 percent at 222.90 francs in a falling market.

Officials at Sommer-Allibert said they knew of no reason for the stock movement, but recalled that finance director Philippe Chaubeau has said the group is trying to acquire or link up with a U.S. auto parts business.
"It's clear their capital isn't locked up," said one analyst.
The SIP family-controlled holding company owns 37 percent of the company, the Sommer family holds 5.8 percent directly, and 57.2 percent is held by banks and investors.
Traders said they believed the block trade might be part of the Sommer family stake.
They say it would make sense for Sommer-Allibert to shed the auto parts business, which requires a lot of investment.
